Hi Soojin,

Thanks for sending the standard Redwood DPA. Our legal team has reviewed and attached a redline with three principal areas of concern:

1) Subprocessors: we are requesting a 30-day notice and an explicit right to object to any new subprocessors that will process regulated customer data. If an objected subprocessor cannot be replaced, WillowBank needs the right to suspend processing for the impacted data set.

2) International transfers: the DPA should include express application of the European Commission SCCs (and the UK Addendum where applicable) rather than a general clause. We also want an express commitment that Redwood will cooperate on any additional safeguards required under Schrems II assessments.

3) Data retention & audit evidence: retention of audit logs and forensics for at least seven (7) years for investigation purposes; and an explicit obligation to provide evidence of SOC 2 and penetration test summaries on request.

We have attached our marked-up DPA (WillowBank_DPA_Redline_v1.docx) and a short note from privacy counsel (Redline_notes_WillowBank.pdf). Please confirm whether Redwood can accept SCCs and provide your current subprocessors list and SOC 2 report. We prefer DocuSign for final execution; if possible route the envelope to our Legal (privacy@willowbank.com) and our Information Security lead (dpierce@willowbank.com).

Target timeframe: we are aiming for execution within 10 business days if the parties can agree on transfer language and subprocessor notice mechanics.

Thanks,
Emma Nolan
Senior Counsel — WillowBank

Hi Emma / team — thank you for the redline and notes. Attached is Redwood's annotated response (Redwood_DPA_Legal_Resp_v1.pdf). High-level positions and suggested compromises below: 

1) Subprocessors: Redwood is happy to provide 30-day advance notice. We propose a 15-day objection window instead of 30 days as a commercial compromise and to allow operational continuity; if WillowBank objects, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to offer an alternative; suspension of processing is a very high bar — we can agree to suspension only for demonstrated regulatory requirement and after escalation, not as a routine right.

2) Transfers & SCCs: we can adopt the SCCs as the transfer mechanism where required (EU/UK) and will include language committing to cooperate on additional safeguards assessments. We prefer to keep a flexible clause that references SCCs and Redwood's transfer addendum (so we don't need to amend the base DPA for every jurisdiction). Suggested wording is included in the attached PDF.

3) Retention & evidence: Redwood can commit to retaining security logs for three (3) years as a standard (longer retention can be agreed for specific regulated deployments in the Dedicated/Private product). We will provide SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and a pen-test executive summary. Seven years for logs is atypical for cloud customers and operationally costly; suggest 3 years + narrow exception language for legal holds related to investigations.

Other notes: we request WillowBank accept the DPA as a schedule to the Master Customer Agreement (so we exchange redlines in the DPA only). We also propose a carve-out for aggregated/anonymized telemetry.

If WillowBank can accept the 15-day notice and SCCs plus the SOC2 packet, we should be able to finalize routing for DocuSign within 48 hours thereafter.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Legal_Resp_v1.pdf (PDF, 14 KB)]
